items.title: Confirm you're visa-free
items.detail: Hong Kong (HKSAR) passports enter Korea visa-free for short tourism, and K-ETA is waived through 2026 — there's nothing to apply for.

items.title: File the e-Arrival Card
items.detail: Within 72 hours before arrival, complete it free at e-arrivalcard.go.kr and save the QR/confirmation.

items.title: Check passport & onward ticket
items.detail: Make sure your passport is valid for your stay, and have a return/onward ticket plus your first accommodation address.

items.title: At immigration
items.detail: Show your passport and e-Arrival confirmation; fingerprints and a photo may be taken. Keep it tourism — no paid work on visa-free entry.

documents.title: What to have ready
documents.intro: You don't file a visa application — but have these ready for a smooth entry.

items.t: Paying a 'visa/K-ETA fee' you don't owe
items.d: Right now you need neither a visa nor K-ETA. Scam sites still charge for them — ignore them.
Most visitors must file it (free). Do it within 72 hours of arrival.

items.t: Filing the e-Arrival Card too early
items.d: It expires 72 hours after submission — file it close to your flight, not weeks ahead.

items.a: No — for short-term tourism, Hong Kong SAR passport holders enter Korea visa-free. You do not apply for any tourist visa.
